Right: the five-cycle without the chord (the dashed edge) is itself an odd hole, a chordless cycle of length 5 (in the accent color), so is_perfect_graph() returns False." width="100%"} A graph is *perfect* when, in it and in every induced subgraph, the chromatic number equals the size of the largest clique: the only thing forcing extra colors is a clique that needs them. Bipartite graphs, chordal graphs, comparability graphs, interval graphs and the complements of all of these are perfect. On perfect graphs maximum cliques, maximum independent sets and optimal colorings can be found in polynomial time, problems that are NP-hard in general. By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem (Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas, 2006), a graph is perfect exactly when it contains no *odd hole* (an induced cycle of odd length 5 or more) and no *odd antihole* (the complement of one). This is what is checked. The five-cycle is the smallest imperfect graph: its largest clique is an edge, yet it needs three colors. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is perfect. Graphs with at most four nodes always are. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Bipartite and chordal graphs are accepted immediately, since neither can contain an odd hole or antihole. Otherwise a depth-first search grows induced paths from each node, extending only by nodes adjacent to the path's last node and to nothing else on it, and stops at the first odd induced cycle of length 5 or more; the same search then runs on the complement. Each cycle is searched for only from its smallest node, so the search is fast on the graphs met in practice, but it is exponential in the worst case (the polynomial recognition algorithm of Chudnovsky et al., 2005, runs in O(n⁹) and is not practical). Results match NetworkX's `is_perfect_graph()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Even cycles are bipartite and so perfect; odd cycles of length 5 or more are odd holes: ::: {#eba3fc18 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec {n: ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(n).is_perfect_graph() for n in range(3, 9)} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: True, 4: True, 5: False, 6: True, 7: False, 8: True} ``` ::: ::: A seven-cycle's complement is an odd antihole, so it is not perfect either, though it has no odd hole: ::: {#ecbfd241 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(7).complement().is_perfect_graph() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
